cards.claim: Critical batch size (CBS) scales primarily with data size rather than model size
cards.conditions: Autoregressive transformer language models (85M–1.2B parameters), C4 dataset, Adam optimizer, context length 512
cards.effect: CBS remains nearly invariant when scaling model size with fixed data, but increases when scaling data size with fixed model size
cards.evidence: Controlled experiments: (1) training all models on same Chinchilla target loss for 151M models shows no CBS increase with larger models; (2) training 302M model on varying token counts shows CBS increases with data size; fits power law CBS ∝ N_data^(0.21)
cards.quote: Overall, our results demonstrate that CBS scales primarily with data size rather than model size, a finding we justify theoretically through the analysis of infinite-width limits of neural networks and infinite-dimensional least squares regression.

cards.claim: Proper hyperparameter tuning (momentum and learning rate) is essential for studying large-scale pre-training beyond fixed durations
cards.conditions: Models 85M–1.2B, C4 dataset, Adam optimizer, batch sizes ranging across linear scaling regime and beyond
cards.effect: Enables reaching target validation loss without predefined training duration
cards.evidence: Empirical design methodology: extensive hyperparameter sweeps documented in Appendix A and B; benchmarking of learning rate schedulers
cards.quote: ensuring proper sweeps of momentum and learning rate ( Appendix A ); adopting well-tuned values for the parameter and the exponential weight averaging decay rate , tailored to each batch size ( Appendix B ).

cards.claim: Exponential weight averaging (EWA) improves optimization efficiency especially for large batch sizes
cards.conditions: Language model pre-training on C4, batch sizes ranging from small (256) to large (4096+), Adam optimizer
cards.effect: EWA matches or outperforms cosine and warmup-stable-decay schedules; reduces need to predetermine training duration
cards.evidence: Empirical comparison (Figure 2): constant+EWA strategy benchmarked against schedule-free optimizer, cosine decay, and WSD across batch size range
cards.quote: Our findings further reveal that EWA can trade memory for optimization efficiency in LM pre-training, especially in large-batch regimes. This is useful in scenarios where a target loss must be achieved, but practitioners are uncertain of the exact maximum data size to set up the learning rate schedule for training.

cards.claim: Below critical batch size, approximately linear scaling of batch size reduces steps by proportional factor
cards.conditions: All model sizes and data sizes tested (85M–1.2B parameters, C4 dataset, up to 1.2T tokens implied by Chinchilla)
cards.effect: Below CBS: doubling batch size reduces steps by ~2×; above CBS: doubling batch size reduces steps by <2×
cards.evidence: Formal definition (Definition 1) and empirical scaling curves (Figure 1, 5, 6) showing linear then sublinear regime
cards.quote: Below the CBS, approximately linear scaling is achievable—doubling the batch size can proportionally reduce the number of optimization steps required to reach a target loss. However, beyond this threshold, further increases in batch size would lead to diminishing returns, making it essential to balance computational efficiency with model performance

cards.claim: Different transformer context lengths (512–2048) have similar scaling behavior with batch size
cards.conditions: 151M parameter models, C4 dataset, batch sizes 256–4096, Adam optimizer
cards.effect: Relative optimization efficiency across batch sizes unchanged by context length; justifies use of 512 as standard
cards.evidence: Ablation study (Figure 4, Section 2.3): four context lengths tested, curves overlap
cards.quote: Overall all models in four different context lengths have very similar relative optimization efficiency across various batch sizes and thus justifies our use of 512 for all the experiments.

cards.claim: Increasing model width and depth have similar effects on CBS in compute-optimal training
cards.conditions: Scaling from 151M to 604M parameters via two paths: width increase or depth increase; C4 dataset, Chinchilla token budget
cards.effect: CBS grows similarly whether depth or width is increased; both achieve same efficiency
cards.evidence: Empirical comparison (Figure 3): 604M models created by scaling 151M in width vs depth show overlapping CBS curves
cards.quote: Increasing width and depth has similar effects in critical batch size for compute-optimal pre-training.

cards.claim: In least-squares regression with mini-batch SGD, CBS scales with data size under variance-dominated regime
cards.conditions: Theoretical: well-specified Gaussian linear regression, mini-batch SGD with constant learning rate, capacity and source power-law conditions

cards.claim: Constant learning rate with EWA can achieve competitive performance compared to decaying schedules for target-loss objectives
cards.conditions: LM pre-training on C4, models 85M–1.2B, batch sizes 256–4096, Adam optimizer, various target losses
cards.effect: Constant+EWA matches cosine (at optimal schedule length multiples 0.9–1.1×) and WSD (at 0.1–0.3× of optimal steps)
cards.evidence: Empirical benchmark (Figure 2): constant+EWA compared against schedule-free, cosine, WSD; best performance for large batch sizes
cards.quote: We show that our constant+EWA strategy can match the efficiency of cosine scheduling and WSD, especially for large batch sizes ( Figure 2 ).
